To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the optimization of learning processes in mathematics involves frequent moments that require the transmission of knowledge by teachers.
the optimization of a learning process involves implementing moments of knowledge transmission by the teacher.

(i) the optimization of the teaching/learning process requires frequent explicit transmission of knowledge; (ii) a systematic analysis of the teaching/ learning process reveals that a mixed instructional model, which articulates constructivists and explicitist approaches, is the most effective way to achieve mathematical learning; (iii) the use of mixed models in teaching mathematics is a relevant topic for mathematics education.
In summary, our research is concerned with
overcoming extreme objectivist and constructivist positions, which are currently in opposition in the mathematics education field.
the analysis of the teaching-learning process, which is based on the study of a particular case of instruction in mathematics, in this case, the teaching of probability to prospective teachers.
the analysis of the instructional process in order to identify didactical facts that are not always evident in the teaching and learning of mathematics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the teaching and learning of mathematics is a complex process, and the use of a mixed instructional model is a necessary condition for its optimization.
the instructional model that was implemented in this case study, which was based on a constructivist approach, was not enough to achieve the learning objectives.

the analysis of the instructional process shows that the optimization of learning requires the explicit teaching of knowledge in frequent moments, in addition to the construction of knowledge through the resolution of problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the analysis of a constructivist instructional process reveals the importance of explicit teaching moments to support the learning of mathematics.
it is not possible to overcome the extreme positions of constructivism and objectivism in the design of mathematics instruction, and it would be necessary to consider the use of a mixed model.

the analysis of the teaching process, in this case of a teaching sequence on elementary probability, shows that it is not possible to overcome the extreme positions in teaching, and that it is necessary to use a mixed instructional model to promote mathematical learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the analysis of instructional trajectories allows us to overcome extreme positions that support only one of the two main instructional models in mathematics education.
the analysis of teaching and learning trajectories is a powerful tool to identify and understand the didactical facts that allow to optimize learning processes.

it is possible to design and implement instructional models that are based on constructivist principles, but that also include explicit teaching, and that are able to promote mathematical learning in a significant and efficient way.
